steps.title: Change Em into E
steps.body:
An E chord is E major: E, G# and B. Compare it with Em, which has G instead of G#. Keep the Em positions on strings 5 and 4, and add fret 1 on string 3.

**Why it matters:** A small position change can alter one note and change the chord from minor to major.

steps.title: Read and hear the notes
steps.body: Use open strings 6, 2 and 1; fret 2 on strings 5 and 4; fret 1 on string 3. E’s root stays E; only the G sound becomes G#.

items.prompt: Play E, B, E, G#, B, E together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: Move string 3 between open and fret 1 while keeping the other positions. Compare the sound of Em and E without rushing.

items.prompt: Play E, B, E, G#, B, E together. Use any positions for these notes.
